operations: JSE-listed REIT (JSE:ATT). Flagship: Waterfall City precinct, Midrand (Mall of Africa 130,000m2 retail, Waterfall Corner, Nexus office buildings, logistics hub); plus precincts in George, Pretoria (Lynnwood Bridge), Potchefstroom (MooiRivier Mall) and Stellenbosch. HQ: Nexus Waterfall, 44 Magwa Cres, Waterfall City. GEPF holds ~30% of Waterfall Investment Co.
scale_note: Portfolio value R22.6-25.2bn. Solar PV: 18.5 MWp installed per Sept-2026 FY results (green energy 13.7% of group power, up from 9.1%); earlier figures conflict (homepage still says 1.3 MWp; Mar-2025 said 2.9 MW targeting 7 MW). A power purchase agreement is 'expected to come online next year' (FY2027) per Sept-2026 results - first wheeled PPA, not yet named. Waterfall receives ~180 MW Eskom supply via six substations (2022). Smart Utility Hub real-time metering; municipal recovery ratio 94.6%. Mall of Africa EDGE Advanced (53% energy saving). Nexus 1 = first net-zero-carbon building (GBCSA). No explicit group net-zero date published; strategy 'Horizon 2030'.

operations: JSE-listed residential developer (JSE:BWN), not a REIT - builds and sells sectional-title apartment estates; growing Balwin Annuity arm (Balwin Rentals build-to-rent, fibre, solar, bond origination). HQ 105 Corlett Drive, Melrose, Johannesburg (6-star Green Star, Net Zero Carbon). Estates across Gauteng, Western Cape, KZN incl. Greenpark (Boksburg), The Eastlake (Johannesburg East), Kikuyu and The Whisken; rental pipeline up to 7,300 apartments across six estates.
scale_note: Not a landlord buying bulk electricity for resale in the REIT sense - residents are metered individually; the buyer is the estate/lifestyle-centre load and Balwin Rentals build-to-rent estates. 98 developments / 56,426 apartments built; 39,151 EDGE Advanced-certified apartments (40%+ energy saving); 10-11 lifestyle centres + HQ rated six-star Green Star Net Zero Carbon. Solar: SolarAfrica partnership (Mar 2025) puts solar on Kikuyu and The Whisken under a no-capex model (size not published); solar+bond-origination annuity revenue R18.7m (H1 FY2026, +60%). No MW total, no wheeling deal and no group Scope 2 target published.

operations: JSE-listed REIT (JSE:EMI), Castleview Property Fund is the controlling shareholder. HQ 1st Floor Building A Knightsbridge, 33 Sloane St, Bryanston, Johannesburg. ~84-90 directly held SA properties (urban retail 43%, office 25%, industrial 15%, residential 17% via Transcend), mostly Gauteng with Western Cape and KZN; flagship Wonderpark Shopping Centre (Pretoria North); plus US and Polish (DL Invest) offshore stakes.
scale_note: Direct SA portfolio ~R12.1bn. Solar: thirteen solar PV farms totalling 12.2 MWp, 21% of commercial portfolio has access to renewable energy (emira.co.za, figure from site search summary - not pinned to a dated page); FY2025 added 5 farms/1.5 MWp, FY2026 plan 8 projects/6 farms/1 MWp; Wonderpark plant expanded to 3.8-4.4 MWp. 79% of commercial GLA has full backup power. Wheeling: CEO said in Jun 2023 that 'wheeling energy produced by independent suppliers' is among alternatives being considered - no wheeling deal announced. First SA REIT with Energy Performance Certificates (2022). CDP reporter since 2011; RMB sustainability-linked loan. No explicit net-zero date found.

operations: JSE-listed specialist logistics REIT (JSE:EQU). Offices: Portside Tower, 4 Bree St, Cape Town (HQ) and Equites Park, Linbro Park, Johannesburg. Prime A-grade distribution centres in Gauteng, Western Cape (Parow, Atlantic Hills), KZN; tenants incl. Shoprite, Pepkor, TFG, DSV; UK portfolio being disposed (2025) to focus on SA.
scale_note: Portfolio R28.3bn (Aug 2025), 616,422m2 green-certified. Most advanced REIT on wheeling: since 1 May 2024 wheels solar from a 17,653m2 Parow DC onto the City of Cape Town grid to supply an offtaker on the Foreshore (CoCT wheeling pilot). Solar 27.0 MW across 37 buildings (Oct 2025; 26.7 MW at Feb 2025), >two-thirds of portfolio solar-supplied; 9 PPAs concluded (Equites sells power to its tenants); 1.2 MW more in 2H26 and +5 MW over 2-3 years; 750,000m2 roof still available; actively seeking more municipal wheeling capacity. SBTi emissions targets adopted (no figure published in results). Note: as a seller of wheeled power Equites is partly a competitor/partner rather than pure offtaker.

operations: JSE-listed REIT (JSE:FFA/FFB), Fortress Real Estate Investments Ltd. HQ Block C, Cullinan Place, Cullinan Close, Morningside, Sandton. Logistics parks (Clairwood Logistics Park Durban, Eastport, Louwlardia, Cornubia, Longlake) and convenience/commuter retail (Park Central, Venda Plaza, AbaQulusi Plaza, Balfour Mall acquired 2026); ~24% stake in NEPI Rockcastle; CEE logistics parks in Poland/Romania.
scale_note: Best-documented decarbonisation programme in the sector: 121 operational solar PV plants at 30 Jun 2026 (133 by Jun 2027), 40.11 MWac installed (38.84 MWac/113 plants at May 2026; 22.17 MWac/59 plants at Jun 2024), ~50,334 MWh solar generated Jul 2025-May 2026 (26.6% up); 100 million kWh cumulative since 2017; R337.9m invested by FY2024. Battery 1.95 MWh installed, 5.1-7.05 MWh ordered. Annual consumption ~246,141 MWh (FY2024). Wheeling: 10-year wheeling agreement with Discovery Green covering 14 Eskom-supplied properties, supplying 70-100% of load not met by on-site solar. Renewable penetration 9% (Jun 2024) -> 18% (Jun 2025) -> 23% target 2026. 2030 target: 45% cut in Scope 1+2+3 vs 2018 baseline.

operations: Largest SA primary REIT (JSE:GRT). HQ The Place, 1 Sandton Drive, Sandton; regional offices Umhlanga and Claremont. 468 property assets group-wide (R157.5bn, 6.9m m2); SA directly held portfolio R65.6bn, 302 properties (FY2026). Flagships: 50% of V&A Waterfront (Cape Town), Sandton/Rosebank/Umhlanga offices, Brooklyn Mall, Walmer Park, Waterfall Mall, N1 City, logistics parks; also Growthpoint Australia, Globalworth (CEE), Lango (Africa); GIP healthcare and student REITs.
scale_note: Sector leader on wheeling: 195 GWh/yr PPA with Etana Energy (signed Jan 2024, 32% of consumption at signing; wind+hydro+solar, wheeled via Eskom grid; commercial ops from 1 Jul 2025, fully implemented by FY2028); exclusive offtake of ~30 GWh/yr from Serengeti's 5 MW Boston hydro. May 2026: first pooled renewable wheeling with City of Cape Town (5 buildings, expanding to 30+). Wheels to 25 SA properties incl. 9 e-CO2 buildings. Rooftop solar 69.31 MWp across 98 plants (FY2026; >R1bn spent since 2011). Renewable penetration 19.0% FY2026 (7.9% FY2025). Target: all buildings net-zero carbon by 2050. Generic procurement@growthpoint.co.za published.

operations: JSE-listed specialist shopping-centre REIT (JSE:HYP), internally managed. HQ 2nd Floor, Cradock Heights, 21 Cradock Ave, Rosebank, Johannesburg. SA portfolio ~R42bn group: Canal Walk (Cape Town, 80%, in talks to buy remaining 20% from Ellerine family), Somerset Mall, CapeGate, Table Bay Mall (acquired 2024), Rosebank Mall, Hyde Park Corner, Clearwater Mall, The Glen, Woodlands Boulevard; Eastern Europe (Croatia, Serbia, N. Macedonia, Bulgaria, Montenegro) ~30% of portfolio value.
scale_note: Solar PV 21,975 kWp installed across SA portfolio (Jun 2026; 18,773 kWp at Jun 2025 across six centres: Clearwater 5,717, Woodlands 5,296, Table Bay 4,386, Rosebank 1,891, The Glen now 4,304, Hyde Park 384), meeting up to 17% of SA energy requirements; FY2025 solar output 23.76 GWh vs grid/Eskom 154.0 GWh. Pipeline: CapeGate 5,337 kWp, Canal Walk 6,650 kWp, Somerset Mall 4,200 kWp, two Croatian sites; BESS feasibility under way. Rosebank Mall hybrid (4.5 MW inverter, 7.2 MWh battery, 3 MW dual-fuel gen) commissioned 2025. Wheeling: NO deal signed - Hyprop received a proposal (HY2025) to supply wheeled energy to its four Western Cape centres contingent on embedded solar at Canal Walk/Somerset, planned wheeling RFPs Jun 2025, but FY2025 ESG report concluded self-financed solar + BESS is the most feasible route (PPAs investigated and set aside). Reports Scope 1-3 (Scope 3 tenants = 77%); no dated net-zero target published; MSCI ESG AA.

operations: Burstone Group Ltd (JSE:BTN) - formerly Investec Property Fund; management internalised from Investec and rebranded Burstone in Oct 2023; now an integrated real-estate investor and fund/asset manager (SA, Europe via PEL/Blackstone and ELI/Hines, Australia via Irongate). HQ 4 Sandown Valley Crescent, Sandown, Sandton. SA portfolio: 52 properties, R13.6bn, 781,807m2 GLA across retail, office and industrial (e.g. Alrode Multipark, 30 Jellicoe Rosebank; Balfour Mall sold to Fortress 2026); SA Core Plus platform being seeded with ~R5bn of SA retail/industrial assets.
scale_note: SA solar 22.7 MWp installed at 31 Mar 2026 (13.1 MWp at Mar 2025; +9.8 MW/+55% in FY26 at ~35% gross yields; R198m invested since 2016; solar on 25+ properties). SA energy consumption 125.7 GWh (FY26). No wheeling or PPA published - solar is self-funded on-site. Targets: 'net-zero emissions by 2050, or earlier'; reports Scope 1-3 for SA; CDP C-rating; 45 Green Star buildings; first SA REIT with a sustainability-linked bond (2021). Smart metering across portfolio.

commodity: retail (super-regional malls) + office/hotel; Eris: diversified managed portfolio
operations: TWO UNRELATED ENTITIES ON ONE RECORD. (1) Liberty Two Degrees (L2D): delisted from JSE 14 Nov 2023 after Liberty Group (wholly owned by Standard Bank Group) bought out minorities at R5.55/share; now 'an asset management business line in the Insurance and Asset Management (IAM) business unit of the Standard Bank Group, appointed as the asset manager of the Liberty Property Portfolio' (operating co: 2 Degrees Properties). Co-owns with Liberty/Pareto: Sandton City complex, Nelson Mandela Square, Eastgate complex, Melrose Arch, Liberty Midlands Mall (Pietermaritzburg), Liberty Promenade (Mitchells Plain), Botshabelo Mall, Sandton Sun/Towers hotels, Sandton Convention Centre; portfolio ~R8.3bn (2023), occupancy 95.3% (Jun 2026). Counterparty for a PPA = Liberty Group Ltd / Standard Bank IAM (Sandton City owners named as Liberty Group and Pareto). (2) Eris Property Group: private developer/manager, 73.75% Momentum Group, HQ The Marc, 129 Rivonia Rd, Sandton; manages ~1.36m m2 GLA incl. Momentum Direct Property Fund's 14 retail centres.
scale_note: L2D: Landlord Scope 1+2 net-zero carbon by 2030 target. Solar 13 MW installed (Sep 2024; 3 MW in 2022), targeting 16.1 MW by end-2025 (~18% of mall consumption): Eastgate 6 MWac/7.216 MWp (SA's largest registered rooftop, 35% of centre load), Midlands Mall ~5 MW, Promenade 1 MW, Sandton City 1 MW (May 2024), Nelson Mandela Square 0.3 MW planned. Wheeling: Sandton City (Liberty Group + Pareto) announced Nov 2024 intent to procure wheeled renewable energy via the Independent Energy Pool (IEP) platform - roof-constrained, so wheeling is the route to 2030 target; no signed supplier announced. 2026 targets: 5% cut in non-renewable energy, 3% water, >90% waste diversion. Eris/Momentum Direct Property Fund: solar at 7 of 14 retail centres by 2022 (>7,000 MWh/yr; Taung Mall 700 kW), plan all 14 by 2030 (17,710 MWh/yr); Momentum net-zero 2050; CEO said wheeling legislation 'will assist us'.
status_flag: delisted - now Liberty Group (Standard Bank Group); Eris Property Group separately active (Momentum Group)

operations: SA's second-largest listed REIT (JSE:RDF). HQ 155 West, 4th Floor, 155 West St, Sandown, Sandton; regional offices Cape Town (Black River Park), Durban, Nelspruit, Polokwane. Group property assets R101-103bn, ~65% SA / 35% Poland (EPP, ELI). SA portfolio R66.5bn, ~3.66m m2 GLA, ~221 properties: retail R30.6bn/54 properties (Centurion Mall super-regional, Maponya Mall, Blue Route Mall, Kenilworth Centre, Alice Lane precinct), office R22.4bn/86 (90 Rivonia, Convention Tower CT), industrial R13bn/82 (Brackengate 2 etc).
scale_note: Most active REIT on wheeling after Growthpoint: (1) 20-year, 37 GWh/yr wheeling agreement with NOA Trading signed Jun 2025 covering 11 Eskom-connected properties, sourced partly from Khauta Solar (Free State); municipal-wheeling phase 2 to follow; brokered by SOLINK. (2) City of Cape Town wheeling pilot - with VDMV, 5.7 MWp rooftop at Massmart Brackengate 2 wheels to Convention Tower (first CT building to receive wheeled green power). (3) HY2026: 18.5 MWh wheeled under short-term PPAs; COO says a short-term 8 MWp offtake concluded and a 20-year 17 MWp wheeling offtake signed, effective early 2027. Rooftop solar 62.23 MWp SA (Feb 2026; retail 47.79, industrial 8.23, office 6.21) - 'largely complete' once 5.6 MWp pipeline done, so growth must come from wheeling/BESS/carports; 7 MW in Poland. Renewable share: office 100%, logistics 100%, retail 35% (FY2025). Net-zero 2030 goal for landlord emissions; 9 Net Zero Carbon Level 2 buildings; 5,000+ smart meters; tenant electricity = 92% of emissions; GRESB 81.

operations: JSE-listed retail REIT (JSE:RES), co-founded by Des de Beer (now non-exec). HQ 4th Floor, Rivonia Village, Rivonia Boulevard, Rivonia (Sandton). 28 dominant regional/rural shopping centres, ~1.2m m2 GLA: Galleria Mall (Amanzimtoti), Irene Village Mall and The Grove Mall (Pretoria), Boardwalk Inkwazi (Richards Bay), Mahikeng Mall, Mams Mall, Jubilee Mall, Brits Mall, Kathu Village Mall, Limpopo Mall, The Crossing Mokopane, Highveld Mall, Diamond Pavilion, Arbour Crossing, Tzaneen Lifestyle Centre; offshore stake in Lighthouse Properties (France/Iberia).
scale_note: Highest on-site solar penetration in the sector and explicitly NOT wheeling: solar installed at ALL shopping centres - 88.0 MWp at Dec 2025 (76.5 MWp Dec 2024; 59.9 MWp Dec 2023), 6.4 MWp more approved for FY2026 to reach 94.4 MWp supplying ~43.2% of total electricity (39.8% at 88 MWp). Boardwalk Inkwazi 6.8 MWp is among SA's largest rooftops. Strategy has shifted to BESS: 30.7 MWh installed at Jun 2026 (20.7 MWh Dec 2025), 27.2 MWh approved for FY2026 (Brits, Jubilee, Kathu, Limpopo, Mams, Mokopane, +2 MWh Irene); automated micro-grids at Irene Village and The Grove. R304.9m spent on energy projects FY2024. Energy strategy 'shields earnings' from Eskom cost-reflective tariff reform. No wheeling or PPA announced and no dated net-zero target published; remaining ~57% of load is grid-supplied - the wheeling opportunity.

operations: JSE-listed, internally managed, Western Cape-only REIT (JSE:SEA). HQ 2nd Floor, Unit 1, No1 Waterhouse, Century City, Cape Town. Portfolio R7.1-8.4bn, 40-42 properties, ~625,000-670,000m2 GLA (industrial ~42% by GLA: Mega Park Bellville, Consani Industrial Park, Berg River Business Park Paarl, GTX Park George, Bravo Blackheath; commercial: No1 Waterhouse, Santam Precinct; retail: Maynard Mall, Watergate Centre). Falls almost entirely under City of Cape Town electricity supply.
scale_note: Solar PV on 27-28 of ~40 assets (2 more under construction, completion Q1-Q2 FY2027); 10.1 MW installed at FY2025 with 12.5 MW target FY2026; average solar penetration ~20-24% of portfolio kWh (top 3 assets = 50% of group kWh at 31% penetration); solar sold to tenants as roof rental - R31.3m revenue / R21.8m NOI FY2026. Wheeling: none signed; FY2025 integrated report says three City of Cape Town wheeling projects were under feasibility to serve assets unsuitable for rooftop solar. ESG framed as 'People, Planet, Profit'; R230m sustainability-linked loan; no dated net-zero target published.

operations: JSE-listed retail REIT (JSE:VKE, also NSX). HQ 11 Ninth Street, Houghton Estate, Johannesburg. SA portfolio R19.5bn (FY2026) of ~33 township, rural, urban and commuter malls (East Rand Mall, Mall of Mthatha, Atlantis Mall, Chatsworth Mall 50% (2026), Botshabelo Mall (2026), Pine Crest, Dobsonville, Phoenix Plaza etc.) plus ~60% of Iberian Castellana Properties (Bonaire, Lar España stake).
scale_note: Solar PV 40.3 MWp across 45 PV projects at Mar 2026 (36 MWp/39 plants Mar 2025; 21.6 MWp Mar 2024) generating 29% of portfolio electricity; 7.3 MWp under construction; target +10 MWp to 46 MWp by FY2028. BESS at 17 centres guaranteeing 9am-4pm tenant supply (R350m programme 2023). Wheeling: NOT yet signed - FY2025 said 'finalising agreements for two wheeling projects totalling 2MWp'; FY2026 (Jun 2026) says Vukile 'is negotiating a final PPA with the preferred renewable energy trader' (savings ~R250k/yr) - i.e. RFP already run. Targets: Scope 1+2 kept below 2,000 tCO2e avg FY25-FY28 on stable portfolio (88% cut over 3 yrs, Scope 2 'eliminated' in stable portfolio via green procurement); 30% of SA retail GLA green-certified by FY28; R4.7bn green/sustainability-linked debt tied to PV and BESS KPIs. Cost-to-income 12.4% credited to electricity savings.

operations: TWO UNRELATED PRIVATE DEVELOPERS ON ONE RECORD. (1) Zenprop Property Holdings: private investor-developer founded 1998, HQ 8th Floor, 140 West Street, Sandton (Cape Town office); sold 26 properties/397,273m2 to Investec Property Fund (now Burstone) for R7.1bn in 2015; co-developed Discovery HQ 1 Discovery Place (45%, with Growthpoint); current flagships incl. Riverlands precinct, Observatory, Cape Town (Amazon Africa HQ 40,000m2, 5-Star Green Star Sustainable Precinct) and Sandton offices. (2) Abland Property Developers: founded 1990, HQ 1st Floor, 16 Mill Street, Stellenbosch (Gauteng office Hertford Office Park, Midrand; Guernsey office); develops and usually sells/co-owns: Sandton Gate (with Tiber), Loftus Park (with Pivotal/Attacq), Irene Link Precinct Centurion (85,000m2, with Giflo and SOM), Rietvlei Precinct (187,000m2 industrial), Groot Phesantekraal View Durbanville (30,000m2 retail), Canal Plaza Century City, Bayer Witfontein (Riverfields), Botfontein Park; Fourways Mall turnaround involvement. Neither is a landlord that resells electricity at REIT scale - both are precinct developers whose managed precincts (Riverlands, Irene Link, Sandton Gate) are the offtake points.
scale_note: Zenprop: no portfolio GLA, solar MW or targets published; first rooftop PV 88 kWp Woodmead 2013 with plans for more; Riverlands precinct is 5-Star Green Star Sustainable Precinct with Amazon 6-star fit-out (2025). Abland: no solar MW or wheeling published; commits all Sandton Gate commercial buildings to min 4-Star Green Star, Irene Link buildings 4-5 Star; Eyethu (Soweto) centre solar-powered; precincts marketed with backup power and water. No net-zero targets published by either. Both private - no integrated reports.
